So it's essentially PS4.5? I dread the kinds of console parity deals Sony and Microsoft are imposing on devs trying to release their games on consoles as well as on PC. Imagine trying to explain angry console gamer pointing out differences between game's PC and console version that just because their console can upscale native 720p/900p to 4K, it doesn't make it look any better.
I've heard of devs nerfing their games' visual quality on PC because PC just far outstripps Console.

That's what "console parity deal" is. I know only of M$ forcing this on devs that want the permit to publish their game on Xbone (if they also have PC version - look at TW3), but I imagine Sony is no different.

The games first and foremost have to run well on the lowest common denominator, so often times you have to primarily develop for the weakest platform (ie the PS3 last gen, Wii the gen before that and XBone current gen). Most studios do not have the time or money to make unique assets for PC vs Console, so many games will use the same assets across the board. It's common to just enable some extra post processing, tweak a few settings, allow higher resolutions or allow a couple more particles to spawn on the PC build.

In the end of the day, publishers do not want to pay developers extra money to develop two versions of the same game.

Source: I'm a console game developer
